text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Acting Prime Minister Ensour meets Palestinian negotiator Abu Mazen and affirms Jordan's support for Palestinian rights.
- Negotiations for merger of Housing Bank and Union Bank for Savings and Investments.

- King Hussein meets U.S. Secretary of State Albright, Commerce Secretary Daley and Arab ambassadors in Washington. Confirmation of need to for activation of peace process and resumption of negotiations on all tracks.

- Government sources say a law covering 1997 elections will be passed as a temporary law without recalling parliament. Parliamentary speaker says government must attract national support for any changes it proposes.
- Jordan and U.S. to sign investment agreements today, Jordanian goods to get special status in U.S.

- Government sources expect that under plans for administrative reforms 60 percent of state workers will compete for remaining jobs, 20 percent will be retrained and another 20 percent will get early retirement.
- Iraqi Defence Minister treated in Amman.
- Export licence requirements to be lifted from April 10 for most Jordanian goods, trade and industry official says.
